variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Start every episode in A (press the first button). First update memory for this step (in particular buttons_pressed, using the press signs named in the memory instruction: the phrase 'is pressed down', or the gripper on a button at height 0.035 or lower with fingers closed, usually with two containers swapping). Then apply the first matching rule: 1. If buttons_pressed is 0: A. 2. If buttons_pressed is 1: B. 3. If the scene at this decision step shows a container 'held in the gripper': D (put down the container). 4. If buttons_pressed is 2, nothing is held, and picked_colors is empty: C, pointing at the memory position (<color>_container) of the FIRST cube color named in the goal instruction (the one after 'hiding the'). Use the remembered container position, not the cube's original spot. 5. If buttons_pressed is 2, nothing is held, picked_colors has one entry, and the goal names a second cube ('another container hiding the ...'): C, pointing at the memory position of that SECOND color. This is the container that has not been lifted yet; do not point at the one just put down. 6. If every cube named in the goal is already in picked_colors and nothing is held: the task is done; answer D. Fallback: if the needed color's memory position is unknown, point C at the container nearest that cube's last known position; if no rule fits at all, answer the next unfinished item in goal order (A, B, C, D).

fields.name: buttons_pressed
fields.description: Carried-in count plus 1 if any execution frame shown at this step either reports a button 'is pressed down' or shows the gripper within a few pixels of a button's listed position at height 0.035 or lower with fingers closed (two containers gliding and swapping in neighbouring frames confirms the same press); otherwise the carried-in count. Count at most one press per step. Start at 0. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Count of button presses completed so far. A press is shown by any execution frame at this decision step in which either a button is reported 'is pressed down', or the gripper stands within a few pixels of a button's listed position at height 0.035 or lower with fingers closed (two containers gliding and swapping in neighbouring frames confirms the same press). At most one press is counted per step. 0 at step #1, 1 at the step after the first press (the one that also shows the container shuffle), 2 from the step after the second press to the end. e.g. 1

fields.name: green_container
fields.description: [y, x] of the container hiding the green cube. If a frame shows the green cube uncovered and no containers, write the cube's position. In the step where containers appear, the field becomes the position of the container standing on the carried-in green position, even if that container never moves. Then follow that container through the frames shown: match each container to the nearest container in the previous frame; during a button press two containers glide around each other and finish swapped, so after the press the green container sits where the other moving container started. Write its position in the last frame shown. Once a frame shows the green cube exposed beneath a container held in the gripper, write the cube's last visible position and freeze the field; a container later set down over the cube does not update it. Start with the cube position seen at the first step. e.g. [136, 108]
fields.annotation: Current [y, x] of the container hiding the green cube. At step #1 (before any container exists) it is the green cube's own position. From the step where containers appear, it is the position of the container that came down on the green cube, then followed frame by frame through every shuffle: during each button press two containers glide around each other and end up having swapped places, so the green container's position becomes the other mover's resting position. Updated at every step to the last frame shown. Once this container has been lifted and the green cube is seen exposed beneath it, the field becomes the cube's last visible position and freezes there; a container later set down over the cube does not change it. e.g. [136, 108]

fields.name: red_container
fields.description: [y, x] of the container hiding the red cube, kept exactly as green_container: cube position before containers exist; from the step where containers appear, the container standing on the carried-in position (even one that never moves), followed frame to frame (two movers during a press swap places), written at the last frame shown; once the red cube is seen exposed beneath a container held in the gripper, the cube's last visible position, frozen regardless of any container later set down over it. e.g. [100, 166]
fields.annotation: Current [y, x] of the container hiding the red cube, kept exactly like green_container: cube position at step #1, then the container that covered it, tracked through each press-time shuffle (the two moving containers swap places), updated to the last frame shown at each step; once the red cube has been seen exposed beneath its lifted container, the field freezes at the cube's last visible position and a container later set down over it does not change it. e.g. [100, 166]

fields.name: blue_container
fields.description: [y, x] of the container hiding the blue cube, kept exactly as green_container: cube position before containers exist; from the step where containers appear, the container standing on the carried-in position (even one that never moves), followed frame to frame (two movers during a press swap places), written at the last frame shown; once the blue cube is seen exposed beneath a container held in the gripper, the cube's last visible position, frozen regardless of any container later set down over it. e.g. [120, 181]
fields.annotation: Current [y, x] of the container hiding the blue cube, kept exactly like green_container: cube position at step #1, then the container that covered it, tracked through each press-time shuffle (the two moving containers swap places), updated to the last frame shown at each step; once the blue cube has been seen exposed beneath its lifted container, the field freezes at the cube's last visible position and a container later set down over it does not change it. e.g. [120, 181]

history.critique:
field buttons_pressed, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Situation: on every episode the frames of the first press never contain the phrase 'is pressed down'; the press is visible only as the gripper descending onto a button (height about 0.03 or lower, fingers closed, button listed a few pixels off its rest spot) while two containers glide and swap. The rule said the count rises when an 'is pressed down' frame appears, so the value it describes (0) differs from the value filled in (1). This breaks PREDICTABILITY. Change: buttons_pressed is the count of presses completed, where a press is any execution frame shown at this step in which either a button is reported 'is pressed down', or the gripper stands within a few pixels of a button's position at height 0.035 or lower with fingers closed. 0 at the first step, 1 at the step after the first press (the one that also shows the container shuffle), 2 from the step after the second press to the end. e.g. 1

field red_container, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Situation: after the red container had been lifted and the red cube seen beneath it, the container was set back down over the cube in the last frames before the next decision. The rule said both 'write the exposed cube's position' and 'update to the last frame shown', so two values were possible for one step. This breaks PREDICTABILITY. Change: once a cube of this color has been seen exposed (its container held in the gripper, cube visible), the field holds the cube's last visible position and freezes there; a container later put down over it does not change the field. Before that event the field is the covering container's position in the last frame shown, tracked through each press-time swap. The same freezing applies to green_container and blue_container. e.g. [100, 166]

field green_container, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Same freezing clause as red_container: once the green cube has been seen exposed, keep its last visible position and ignore any container later set down over it. e.g. [136, 108]

field blue_container, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Same freezing clause as red_container: once the blue cube has been seen exposed, keep its last visible position and ignore any container later set down over it. e.g. [120, 181]

field buttons_pressed, POLICY PROMPT
  Situation: at the decision step after the first press, no frame carried the phrase 'is pressed down', the only signs being the gripper at the button's position at height 0.025 with fingers closed and the containers shuffling; the policy kept 0 while the recorded value was 1, then answered the first-button press again. This breaks PREDICTABILITY (and through it SUFFICIENCY). Change: carried-in count plus 1 if any execution frame shown at this step either reports a button 'is pressed down' or shows the gripper within a few pixels of a button's listed position at height 0.035 or lower with fingers closed (containers gliding and swapping in neighbouring frames is a confirming sign of the same press). Count at most one press per step. Start at 0. e.g. 1

field red_container, POLICY PROMPT
  Situation one: when the containers first appeared the policy left the field at the red cube's old position instead of the container standing on it. Situation two: after the red cube was exposed, the container was put back down over it and the policy wrote the put-down container's position while the recorded value kept the cube's last visible position. Both break PREDICTABILITY. Change: before containers exist, the red cube's position. In the step where containers appear, the field becomes the position of the container standing on the carried-in position, for every color including a container that never moves. Then follow that container frame to frame (match each container to the nearest one in the previous frame; during a press two movers swap places) and write the last frame shown. Once a frame shows the red cube exposed beneath a container held in the gripper, write the cube's last visible position and freeze the field; a container later set down over the cube does not update it. e.g. [100, 166]

field green_container, POLICY PROMPT
  Kept exactly like red_container, including: becomes a container position as soon as containers appear even if that container never moves, and freezes at the cube's last visible position once the green cube has been seen exposed. e.g. [136, 108]

field blue_container, POLICY PROMPT
  Kept exactly like red_container, including: becomes a container position as soon as containers appear even if that container never moves, and freezes at the cube's last visible position once the blue cube has been seen exposed. e.g. [120, 181]

variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Start every episode in A (press the first button). First update memory for this step (in particular buttons_pressed, using the press signs named in the memory instruction: the phrase 'is pressed down', or the gripper on a button at height 0.035 or lower with fingers closed, usually with two containers swapping). Then apply the first matching rule: 1. If buttons_pressed is 0: A. 2. If buttons_pressed is 1: B. 3. If the scene at this decision step shows a container 'held in the gripper': D (put down the container). 4. If buttons_pressed is 2, nothing is held, and picked_colors is empty: C, pointing at the memory position (<color>_container) of the FIRST cube color named in the goal instruction (the one after 'hiding the'). Use the remembered container position, not the cube's original spot. 5. If buttons_pressed is 2, nothing is held, picked_colors has one entry, and the goal names a second cube ('another container hiding the ...'): C, pointing at the memory position of that SECOND color. This is the container that has not been lifted yet; do not point at the one just put down. 6. If every cube named in the goal is already in picked_colors and nothing is held: the task is done; answer D. Fallback: if the needed color's memory position is unknown, point C at the container nearest that cube's last known position; if no rule fits at all, answer the next unfinished item in goal order (A, B, C, D).
